# Keep one project reference

## Project interpretation
A billing document has one project-reference slot in the semantic model. In a
credit note, that reference is represented through a specially typed additional
document reference; adding a second one creates another project reference rather
than extra description for the first.

## Common causes
- Several project codes from a source record were exported independently.
- An existing reference was appended instead of replaced during an update.
- A generic supporting-document loop emitted more than one project-typed entry.

## Safe fix
Select the single project that the billing document actually concerns. If other
references are needed, map them only to their correct business terms rather than
labelling them as projects. The corrected synthetic credit note removes the
duplicate and is revalidated in full.

## Failing fragment
```xml
<cac:AdditionalDocumentReference>
  <cbc:ID>PROJ-A</cbc:ID>
  <cbc:DocumentTypeCode>50</cbc:DocumentTypeCode>
</cac:AdditionalDocumentReference>
<cac:AdditionalDocumentReference>
  <cbc:ID>PROJ-B</cbc:ID>
  <cbc:DocumentTypeCode>50</cbc:DocumentTypeCode>
</cac:AdditionalDocumentReference>
```

## Corrected fragment
```xml
<cac:AdditionalDocumentReference>
  <cbc:ID>PROJ-A</cbc:ID>
  <cbc:DocumentTypeCode>50</cbc:DocumentTypeCode>
</cac:AdditionalDocumentReference>
```
